meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale, and I'd like to know why my son found out he got a zero from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of a class.
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, Hale, and on what basis?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
I'm writing down what you said. Procedure 4.2 says you call me before any mark goes in, and you didn't, so what did you do about 4.1 and 4.3 before you entered it?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
A student can misquote a line from memory, Hale. Turn the screen, I'll search the scene myself.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.
That's 4.4, and I want it in writing tonight, along with the zero coming out of the gradebook until then. I'm still waiting to search that scene myself, Hale.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You offered a supervised rewrite under 4.4 on Thursday at 8:15 in your room with the vice-principal, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing going on Owen's record. I still require that offer in writing tonight, the zero removed from the gradebook until then, and the chance to search the scene myself. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: the principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She finished at her fallback, having said your 4.4 offer was what she wanted in writing, but she had not yet accepted the rewrite, and she still wants the zero out of the gradebook and the chance to search the scene herself; a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record is the fair outcome, and you are close to it.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in one sentence and then gave her dated, checkable material, which got her to ask real questions instead of attacking.
What cost ground: You offered the rewrite before she had checked the scene, so she held her demand that the zero come out and kept pressing on procedure.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history of a late-night start the night before it was due came close to that night, but it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked to search the scene, turn the screen and let her do it before you move to the rewrite.
